artifact_observations.reasoning: The white cable emerging from the bottom of the iPod does not connect to a standard 3.5mm jack plug. Instead, it seems to merge directly into the casing or terminate in a strange, thickened, non-functional bulbous shape that lacks the geometry of a real audio connector.

The cable has a distinct segmented or ribbed texture that looks more like a flexible conduit or a stylized drawing than a standard smooth rubber earphone wire. This is a subtle material inconsistency.
The labels on the click wheel (Menu, Next/Prev symbols) appear slightly warped and do not perfectly follow the elliptical perspective of the wheel's surface, suggesting minor texture mapping issues.

To rigorously inspect the connection point between the cable and the device for fusion artifacts and verify the physical continuity of the cable.
To evaluate the realism of the materials (metallic reflections on iPod, leather texture on background) and detect any global coherence issues.
To verify that the iPod sits correctly on the surface with appropriate contact shadows and no floating artifacts.

focus_areas: Connectivity of the earphone jack to the iPod body
Realism of the cable texture and geometry
Clarity and perspective correctness of the click wheel interface
Specular highlights on the metallic/plastic casing
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the earphone cable connection. AI models often struggle with thin cables connecting to ports, resulting in 'melting' or missing plugs. Verify if the cable actually enters a port or just blends into the case. Also, check if the screen content is coherent or just gibberish patterns mimicking text.
